paper_metadata.title: Structure and Properties of Boron- and Zirconium-Inoculated Refractory Nickel Alloys Subjected to HTTM

In both alloys the mean size of macrograins in thin cross sections (as compared to the structure of standard commercial alloys) decreases after the inoculation with boron, HTTM, and inoculation with zirconium (Fig. 1 a and b ).

The long-term strength of specimens with functional zone 5 mm in diameter was evaluated using a DST-500 device at a temperature of 950°C and a stress of 120 MPa (for alloy ZhS3LS-VI) and 850°C and 350 MPa (for alloy ZMI3U-VI).

In both alloys the mean size of macrograins in thin cross sections (as compared to the structure of standard commercial alloys) decreases after the inoculation with boron, HTTM, and inoculation with zirconium (Fig. 1 a and b ).

When the alloys are inoculated with zirconium, carbonitrides of the refractory metals start to be segregated already from the melt and promote hardening of the alloy due to their good thermodynamic stability until at least 1300°C.
The transfer of the eutectic into the /c103-solid solution during heat treatment of the alloy improves the homogeneity of the metal still more.
The effect of high-temperature treatment of melt (HTTM) and born and zirconium inoculation on the structure and properties of castings from nickel refractory alloys ZhS3LS-VI and ZMI3U-VI is studied.
The inoculants were zirconium of grade KTTS-100 (TU 95.2185) and boron in the form of an NB-1 (Ni – B) addition (TU 14-5-106–78).
The inoculants were zirconium of grade KTTS-100 (TU 95.2185) and boron in the form of an NB-1 (Ni – B) addition (TU 14-5-106–78).
The alloys inoculated with boron contain an excess carboboride eutectic (Fig. 2 b ), which means that the content of boron in the alloys exceeds its ultimate solubility in the metallic matrix.

In both alloys the mean size of macrograins in thin cross sections (as compared to the structure of standard commercial alloys) decreases after the inoculation with boron, HTTM, and inoculation with zirconium (Fig. 1 a and b ).

When the alloys are inoculated with zirconium, carbonitrides of the refractory metals start to be segregated already from the melt and promote hardening of the alloy due to their good thermodynamic stability until at least 1300°C.
The specimens of alloy ZhS3LS-VI after HTTM + Zr inoculation exhibited a long time before failure (> 200 h).
Inoculation with boron has not provided the required level of impact toughness and even reduced the elongation and contraction to the lowest values as compared to the other treatment variants.
